the ISC markers are not expressed in serrated polyp lesions and the expression of ISC markers was significantly higher in conventional adenoma than in serrated polypy.
the ISC markers LGR5 and EPHB2 were significantly increased in the serrated polyps compared with the conventional adenomas, and the expression of ASCL2 and OLFMs were not significantly increased.
the ISC markers, LGR5, EPHB4 and OLFM5, were significantly overexpressed in the serrated pathway of CRCs, and the expression of ASCL2 was significantly higher in conventional adenoma.

the distribution of intestinal stem cells markers and their clinical implications in colorectal precancers.
the expression of ISC markers in the precancerous lesions and their clinical implications.

the expression and distribution patterns of LGR5, EPHB4, OLFM4 and ASCL2 are similar in serrated polyp and conventional adenoma, and the expression of LGR5 and EPHB4 is associated with the risk of progression to CRCs.

the expression of ISC markers in colorectal serrated polyps is not consistent with that in adenomas, and the expression of ISC marker is not a reliable predictor of the risk of malignant progression in serrated polyp.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LGR5 and ASCL2 are expressed in the lower third of the serrated polyps, and EPHB2 is expressed in the middle third of the serrate polyps.
the distribution of LGR5+ cells is more extensive in serrated polyp lesions than in adenomas.
LGR5, OLFM4 and EPHB2 are expressed in the lower part of the crypts of serrated polyps, while ASCL2 is mainly expressed in the upper part of the crypt.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LGR5 and ASCL2 were highly expressed in serrated polyp lesions, whereas LGR5, EPHB and OLFM were not detected in adenoma lesions.
LGR5 and ASCL2 expression is not limited to the ISC niche in precancerous polyps, but is also present in the epithelium, which is consistent with their expression in CRCs.
the expression of ISC markers is not restricted to the crypt base but also extends to the middle and even the top of the crypt.
